chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no constriction nor extension except that Allah has therein a will, an ordainment, and a trial.

key_terms.ابْتِلَاءٌ: Trial/test — God's testing of His servants through both hardship and ease
key_terms.بَسْطٍ: Expansion/extension — refers to increase or ease in provision or circumstances
key_terms.قَبْضٍ: Constriction/withholding — refers to reduction or hardship in provision or circumstances
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: Ordainment/decree — divine judicial determination, part of the doctrine of qada wa qadar
key_terms.مَشِيئَةٌ: Divine will/desire — God's absolute sovereign will preceding all acts

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the divine purpose behind constriction and expansion of provision?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that every fluctuation in provision — whether decrease or increase — is not random but is governed by divine will, decree, and divine testing. This hadith, narrated in the chapter on trial and testing, establishes the theological principle that qada (divine ordainment) encompasses all states of human experience, and that constriction and expansion of sustenance are both purposeful acts of God. The audience of Imam al-Sadiq understood 'qabd' and 'bast' as theological terms for all changes in worldly conditions, not merely material wealth.
